summary: mypintusan (the door access-control appliance) can now be discovered, adopted and managed by a myseliasan control plane, on the identical shared node stack mymatasan and myiotsan already use. domain/shared/fleetnode gains a new node kind, KindDoor. On the node side, a new apps/mypintusan/app/wire_fleet.go wires the pairing service, mTLS enrollment, and a two-channel (no media -- a door controller has no video) node-dialed control channel, plus a new apis/notifications.go exposing the unified event feed (including the ?since= replay endpoint myseliasan's reconnect-replay logic pulls from). Every access decision a controller makes (badge grant, badge deny, operator unlock) now also publishes into that feed via a new NotificationAlarmer.Decision, at Info severity -- this is what lets the fleet correlate a door event against camera and sensor events. Duress is deliberately invisible in that published stream: a duress grant's notification is byte-identical to a normal grant's (the reason is normalised to "ok", a bad PIN or duress PIN both coarsen to "credential-rejected", and Detail/RawCredential are never included); the existing Critical duress alarm, worded for an operator, is unaffected and still fires separately. config.json gains a pairing block (mtlsPort 39532, controlPort 39533, matching the suite-wide port convention; no mediaPort). The Settings screen gains a Fleet panel (fleet key, claim code, status, leave-fleet). RBAC policy gains rows for /api/notifications (viewer-read), /api/notifications/*/read (operator-write) and /api/pairing (admin-only, since joining/leaving a fleet changes who can manage a building's doors remotely). Live-bench verified end-to-end: UDP discovery, claim-code adopt, mTLS enrollment, the control channel, an embedded management UI over the tunnel, a badge decision reaching the parent's unified feed, and a remote unlock issued through the tunnel audited on the node as "cp:admin".
compatibility: Backward compatible. mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, so this change ships under the core/infra scope and does not cut a mypintusan release or tag. Fleet pairing defaults to enabled but inert until an operator sets a fleet key and generates a claim code on the node -- an install that never does so behaves exactly as before. The new /api/notifications and /api/pairing routes are additive; existing endpoints, schema, and decision/alarm behavior are unchanged except for the new (additive) Decision publish inside Controller.record, which never affects whether a door opens.
